source_provenance.scope: BBN Lisp DWIM; context-sensitive typo correction including transposition and doubled characters
Interlisp 1986 reference, chapter 22 DWIM automatic error correction and chapter 22.6 spelling corrector
Interlisp course 11: spelling correction and transposition/doubling heuristics

provenance_boundary: Historical references support existence and design motivation of DWIM, NOT identity/equivalence with our deterministic OSA metric or new no-auto-rewrite policy. These are original proposed SENS data-level restrictions.

candidate.output_contract: EXACT/SUGGEST with [surface, exact-identity], AMBIGUOUS with ordered alternatives, ABSENT, or BLOCKED-SURFACE; no execution side effect
candidate.law: Return the unique lowest-distance candidate within an explicit maximum adjacent-transposition edit bound. Exact binary identity is never guessed; equal-score distinct identities produce AMBIGUOUS; bit words or D2 syntax are blocked. Never rewrite or evaluate source.
positive_witnesses: CONNS => CONS if context contains exactly CONS and OSA distance=1
CNOS => CONS by one adjacent transposition
CONX => COND only when the explicitly supplied context lacks another tied candidate such as CONS
Unicode Cyrillic non-binary surface may receive data-only suggestion; no Text7 identity mutation
An exact present label returns EXACT with its pinned bit-identity
negative_falsifiers: CONX with tied COND and CONS at distance=1 is AMBIGUOUS, never arbitrary winner
equal surface with two DIFFERENT bit-identities must be AMBIGUOUS even at distance=0
binary input 01011 must be BLOCKED-SURFACE, never corrected to 01010
source control tokens (., brackets, quotes, spaces) BLOCKED-SURFACE
out-of-bound candidate must be ABSENT, never rewritten or executed
same identity repeated must not spuriously be two alternatives
